CurrentLocation: Archaeological Museum of Delphi, Delphi, Greece
Description: Nine fragments of a letter from Emperor Claudius mentioning Gallio as proconsul of Achaia, reassembled from excavations at Delphi. Because Claudius's reign dates the letter, Gallio's proconsulship can be fixed to about AD 51-52.
BiblicalSignificance: Acts 18 places Paul before Gallio in Corinth during an eighteen-month stay, so the inscription gives one of the firmest dates in Paul's life and helps anchor the whole chronology of Acts. It is a quiet encouragement that Luke wrote careful, checkable history.
Interpretations: Scholars agree the Delphi inscription names Gallio as proconsul of Achaia in AD 51–52, anchoring the date of Paul’s Corinthian ministry in Acts 18.
